findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed to wash their hands, then turn off the faucet with their bare hands. CORRECTED- The employee was educated to use a paper towel to turn off the faucet to avoid recontaminating their freshly washed hands. Ensure that employees are educated on the proper handwashing procedure to prevent contamination to food.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer bucket on the cook-line was observed to have a concentration of 100ppm of Quaternary ammonium. CORRECTED- The sanitizer bucket was remade and tested to be at a concentration of 200ppm of Quaternary ammonium. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are frequently tested and remade if not at a label-recommended concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed an opened roasted garlic Parmesan sauce labeled “Refrigerate After Opening” stored on the kitchen counter and in a serving bowl. CORRECTED - The PIC was instructed that time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods labeled “Refrigerate After Opening” must be stored under refrigeration for safety purposes. The sauce was voluntarily discarded. Ensure all TCS sauces are refrigerated after opening and maintained at 5°C (41°F) or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the following non-food contact surfaces to have crevice and broken parts:

- The kitchen handwashing sink’s caulking is peeling off and needs to be re-sealed.
- The deep reach-in silver freezer cover is partially broken and needs to be replaced.

The PIC was informed and the areas mentioned above would be repaired before the next routine inspection. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are free of crevices or broken parts to allow for easy cleaning.
findings.citation_text: 4-202.16 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed soil accumulation on the caulking around the triple sink in the dry storage area and the handwashing sink at the ice cream station. The PIC was informed that the caulking must be cleaned prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are regularly cleaned and maintained free of soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the following areas of the facility to be in need of repair:

- The back door does not remain closed properly, and light is visible through the bottom right side of the door, which may allow the entry of pests and insects.
- Floor tiles are missing beneath the triple sink.
- Wall tiles at the mop station are loose and separating from the wall.

The PIC was informed, and the issues listed above are to be corrected prior to the next routine inspection. The physical facility must be maintained in good repair at all times.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed mop in the back storage area to be stored in old mop water. PIC was informed that mop water needs to be discarded after use and mop should be stored such that it can drip dry. The mop water was discarded and the mop was stored in the strainer of the bucket during the inspection. Ensure staff are emptying the bucket and storing the mop properly after use.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: Inspector observed a facility practice of putting ranch into cups and holding it in the top of the make table. The back right container had cups of ranch at 50F due to the portion cups being piled up above the fill line in the unit. When pre-portioning food in cups take care to keep the number of cups minimized in the containers so that the food remains cold. Cups lower in the container are 42/43. Keeping the lid closed on the make table when it is not in use is also very important to maintain temperature.  5 cups of ranch were voluntarily discarded. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

(A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.comment:

(A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. C

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: Inspector observed the lid of the burger freezer has cracks which would interfere with cleaning. Repair or replace the sliding door on the burger freezer by the next routine inspection. 

NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: Inspector observed the new sink in the men’s restroom and the hand sink on the line in the kitchen are both missing a silicone seal along the top where the sink meets the wall. Repair/replace/provide silicone seals on these sinks. 

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.comment:
Observed employee turn off the hand sink with bare hands. Use a clean barrier to operate faucet handles. 
Employee was coached and washed hands properly. The violation is corrected on site. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the blade of the can opener to be soiled with dry food debris. The can opener was immediately washed, rinsed and sanitized by an employee.The violation is corrected on site.  

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the seal areas on the front of the low boy soiled. The edge under the lid of the burger chest freezer is also soiled. Clean these areas and maintain them clean. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed personal items in the kitchen on a shelf mixed with food items. the bag and other item was removed. To proper storage. Take care to store personal items properly. Violation was corrected on site. 

6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed no Norovirus illness clean-up policy available for the facility. Facility PIC indicated it was lost. Provided new copy. Facility has bleach to perform procedure. Ensure policy is hung where employees can find it. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following areas no longer smooth and easily cleanable, non-absorbent:
1. Re-caulking needed at the men’s bathroom hand sink and the hand sink near the drive thru window. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 6/26/20 and 4/2/21.
2. Both 3 compartment sinks need re-caulking and/or caulked (moldy and/or missing). 
3. Holes present in the walls above the ice cream 3 compartment sink and the hand sink wall right next to this area. Caulk all holes.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure areas are caulked before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-202.11: Light bulbs shall be shielded, coated or otherwise shatter-resistant in certain areas. 

(REPEAT) Observed the light shield in the prep area/fry line to be broken. Plastic cover over lights needs replaced. Discussed with PIC. Ensure light is corrected by next routine inspection. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 4/2/21.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

(REPEAT) Observed no food handler’s licenses available at the facility. Ensure facility has copies of all food handler’s and CFPM’s licenses on hand at the facility. Ensure new hires obtain the license within 30 days of employment. Keep copies in the public health folder/binder. Discussed with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 6/26/20 and 4/2/21.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements for facility. Provided new copy. Employee's must have signed employee health reporting agreements on file at facility and knowledge of significance of document. Discussed with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 4/12/21.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Observed hand washing sink near ice cream prep area to lack paper towels. Discussed with PIC. COS.

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Observed ladder to be blocking hand washing sink at ice cream prep area. Discussed keeping hand sinks accessible at all times. COS.

6-301.14: A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES. 

Observed hand sink near drive thru to lack a hand washing sign. Men's bathroom lacks a hand washing sign. Provided two hand washing signs for facility. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed both sani buckets to have 100 ppm of quaternary ammonium. Discussed frequent sani bucket changes with PIC. Quat should test between 200-400 ppm. COS.
Observed quat at ice cream prep 3 compartment sink to have 0 ppm. The quat is not coming from the container to the line, then dispensed to the sink. Discussed fixing with PIC. Employee's attempted to fix during inspection - not successful. Inspector instructed facility to only utilized the 3 compartment sink in back until repaired. Inspector will follow-up on 4/6/21.

findings.comment:

(C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.
